text: Replace existing uPVC windows with new double-glazed units in same openings
label: competent_person_scheme
rationale: Replacement windows are controlled fittings; a registered competent person scheme installer can certify them, otherwise apply to a building control body.

text: Replace front door with new door more than half glazed (door and frame)
label: competent_person_scheme
rationale: Regulations apply to a new door only when over 50% of door and frame is glazed; a registered competent person can self-certify, otherwise make an application.

text: Replace external back door with solid door, glazing under 50% of door and frame
label: not_notifiable
rationale: GOV.UK lists external doors with less than half the door glazed among work not needing building regulations approval.

text: Widen existing window opening and fit new lintel and larger window
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
rationale: For new or widened openings an application is needed for the structural opening and lintel even if a competent person fits the window.

text: Install new rooflight in existing pitched roof (cut rafters, trimmers)
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
rationale: Approval is generally needed for a new rooflight because the roof structure must be altered to form the opening and carry the load.

text: Replace existing rooflight with new unit in same opening
label: competent_person_scheme
rationale: Schedule 3 para 10 lets a registered person self-certify replacement windows, rooflights, roof windows or doors in an existing dwelling.

text: Strip and re-cover whole pitched roof with like-for-like tiles
label: competent_person_scheme
rationale: Replacement of roof coverings on pitched and flat roofs is self-certifiable work under NAPIT or CompetentRoofer schemes.

text: Repair small area of roof covering (under 25% of roof, like-for-like)
label: not_notifiable
rationale: Repairs or re-covering affecting under 25% of the envelope and under 50% of the roof normally need no building control application.

text: Inject cavity wall insulation into existing masonry cavity walls
label: competent_person_scheme
rationale: Cavity wall insulation is specifically notifiable; a building notice is required unless a registered installer handles notification.

text: Install external wall insulation and render system to solid walls
label: competent_person_scheme
rationale: Schedule 3 para 19 lists installing insulation to external walls as work a registered person can self-certify.

text: Dry-line inside of external solid walls with insulated plasterboard
label: competent_person_scheme
rationale: Schedule 3 para 18 lists installing insulation to internal walls (excluding flexible thermal linings) as self-certifiable by registered persons.

text: Lay mineral wool loft insulation between and over ceiling joists (insulation only)
label: not_notifiable
rationale: GOV.UK says installing insulation in roof spaces does not need building regulations approval.

text: Insulate under suspended timber ground floor (insulation only, no floor replacement)
label: not_notifiable
rationale: GOV.UK says installing insulation under timber floors does not need building regulations approval.

text: Remove and re-render more than 25% of external wall area
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
rationale: Re-rendering 25% or more counts as renovation of a thermal element needing insulation and a building regulations application.

text: Replace rainwater gutters and downpipes
label: not_notifiable
rationale: GOV.UK lists gutters or downpipes among work not needing building regulations approval.

text: Replace bath, WC and basin like-for-like in same positions
label: not_notifiable
rationale: Like-for-like replacement of bathroom units and fittings does not normally need building control approval.

text: Form new en-suite shower room in bedroom connecting to existing soil stack
label: competent_person_scheme
rationale: A completely new en-suite needs approval; a competent person can self-certify it, otherwise an application is needed.

text: Install whole-house mechanical ventilation with heat recovery (MVHR)
label: competent_person_scheme
rationale: Schedule 3 para 6 lets registered persons self-certify a ventilation or air conditioning system in a dwelling not shared with others.

text: Relocate WC and basin with new connection to underground drain
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
rationale: Relocating bathroom fittings with new connections to a stack or underground drain is controllable work needing approval.

text: Remove loadbearing internal wall and install steel beam on padstones
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
rationale: All structural alterations, including knocking down load-bearing walls, require building regulations approval.

text: Remove non-loadbearing stud wall between lounge and entrance hall/stairs
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
rationale: Taking out a non-loadbearing wall that separates a room from the hall, stair or landing needs a building regulations application.

text: Underpin part of house foundations after subsidence
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
rationale: Underpinning is defined as building work and normally requires building regulations approval with a structural design.

text: Convert loft into habitable bedroom with new stair
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
rationale: Converting a loft into liveable space requires building regulations approval covering structure, fire escape and stairs.

text: Convert integral garage into habitable room
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
rationale: Converting all or part of a garage into habitable space normally requires building regulations approval.

text: Build 20 m2 ground-level conservatory separated by external doors, independent heating
label: not_notifiable
rationale: Ground-level conservatories under 30 m2, separated by external-quality doors with independent heating, are normally exempt.

text: Remove external doors between house and existing conservatory to open plan
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
rationale: Removing exterior doors or walls between the house and a conservatory needs building regulations approval as the exemption is lost.

text: Build 20 m2 garden room with bedroom for guests
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
rationale: Small detached buildings escape the regulations only if they contain no sleeping accommodation.

text: Inject chemical damp-proof course into existing walls
label: not_notifiable
rationale: Installing or replacing a damp-proof course in most instances does not require building regulations approval.

text: Internal redecoration: wallpaper, paint and new skirting boards
label: not_notifiable
rationale: Internal decorating such as wallpapering, painting or new skirting boards does not normally require approval.

text: Replace kitchen units and worktops in same layout
label: not_notifiable
rationale: Refitting a kitchen with new units and fittings does not generally require approval, though drainage or electrics may.

text: New office building
label: full_plans_required
rationale: Brent lists buildings covered by the Fire Safety Order, including offices, shops, factories and workplaces, as needing a full plans application rather than a building notice.

text: Internal alterations to an office that change the means of escape
label: full_plans_required
rationale: Stratford says a building notice cannot be used for non-domestic work affecting means of escape or for non-domestic buildings subject to the Fire Safety Order.

text: Structural alterations during a shop fit-out
label: full_plans_required
rationale: Oxford states a building notice cannot be used for commercial works or premises covered by the Fire Safety Order such as shops, factories and offices.

text: Extension to a factory
label: full_plans_required
rationale: East Staffordshire says building notices cannot be used for offices, shops, hotels, boarding houses or certain factories, so full plans are needed.

text: Alterations to a hotel
label: full_plans_required
rationale: East Staffordshire lists hotels and boarding houses among building uses for which a building notice cannot be used.

text: Alterations to a bed and breakfast guesthouse
label: full_plans_required
rationale: GOV.UK says fire safety law covers workplaces, premises open to the public and paying-guest accommodation such as B&Bs; with reg 12(3) this means full plans.

text: Alterations to a public building such as a community hall
label: full_plans_required
rationale: Oxford lists public buildings among Fire Safety Order premises where a building notice cannot be used.

text: New fire doors and partitions in the common stairwell of a block of flats
label: full_plans_required
rationale: Preston says full plans must always be used for works in the common parts of buildings containing flats and houses in multiple occupation.

text: Alterations to a house in multiple occupation
label: full_plans_required
rationale: Brent requires full plans for residential properties with shared areas, naming flats, maisonettes, hotels and houses in multiple occupation.

text: Work to a converted building containing flats with shared common areas
label: full_plans_required
rationale: Swindon says a building notice cannot be used for flats with common areas or for work to non-domestic buildings.

text: Converting a house into self-contained flats with a shared entrance
context: House being converted to flats in England
label: full_plans_required
rationale: Planning Portal says full plans are always needed where the Fire Safety Order applies or will apply after the work is completed.

text: Change of use of a house to a shop
label: full_plans_required
rationale: Planning Portal says full plans are required where the Fire Safety Order will apply to the building once the work is complete.

text: Work to a workplace or premises where the Fire Safety Order applies
label: full_plans_required
rationale: The partnership says full plans are required where the Fire Safety Order applies, which covers almost all buildings other than private houses and flat interiors.

text: New house fronting onto a private street
label: full_plans_required
rationale: Dover says the building notice route cannot be used for a new building fronting a private street and full plans are needed instead.

text: New building facing a private road
label: full_plans_required
rationale: Brent lists a building facing a private road among cases needing a full plans application.

text: New dwellings on an unadopted estate road
label: full_plans_required
rationale: GOV.UK notes many new dwellings front a private street at application stage, so full plans are needed and a building notice would be invalid.

text: New building on a site fronting a private street
label: full_plans_required
rationale: Hertfordshire Building Control says a full plans application is needed where the property fronts a private road.

text: Rear extension to a house within 3 m of a public sewer
label: full_plans_required
rationale: Brent requires full plans for extensions built over or within three metres of a public sewer.

text: Extension built directly over a public sewer
label: full_plans_required
rationale: Swindon says a building notice cannot be used for work to any building above or within 3 metres of a public sewer.

text: Underpinning a house within 3 m of a public sewer
label: full_plans_required
rationale: East Staffordshire says building notices cannot be used for buildings, extensions or underpinning within 3 metres of a public sewer.

text: New detached building close to a drain shown on the sewer map
label: full_plans_required
rationale: Planning Portal says full plans are required for work built close to or over drains shown on the map of sewers.

text: House extension within 3 m of a public sewer where a build-over agreement is already in place
label: full_plans_required
rationale: Regulation 12(5) requires full plans wherever H4 imposes a requirement, with no exception for work that already has a water company build-over agreement.

text: Extension within 3 m of a non-public sewer shown on the sewer records
label: full_plans_required
rationale: Approved Document H says H4 covers building or extending within 3 m of a drain or sewer on the undertaker's records, public or not.

text: Single-storey rear extension to a house away from sewers and not on a private street
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
rationale: The Hampshire partnership says building notices are generally used for smaller works such as single-storey extensions, subject to the sewer and private street exclusions.

text: Removing one or two internal walls in a house
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
rationale: Oxford lists internal alterations removing one or two walls as suitable straightforward domestic work for a building notice.

text: Underpinning house foundations with no sewer nearby
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
rationale: Sevenoaks says a building notice is only for domestic work and suits smaller jobs such as underpinning, internal alterations or re-roofing.

text: Internal alterations inside a single flat not affecting common parts
label: building_notice_or_full_plans
rationale: The partnership notes the Fire Safety Order does not apply inside individual flats, only to common areas, so the full plans trigger is not met.

text: Replacement windows in an office fitted by a FENSA-registered installer
label: competent_person_scheme
rationale: Schedule 3 paragraph 11 lets registered installers such as FENSA self-certify replacement windows and doors in buildings other than dwellings.

text: Replacement windows in a house fitted by a FENSA-registered installer
label: competent_person_scheme
rationale: Schedule 3 paragraph 10 lets registered installers such as FENSA self-certify replacement windows and doors in existing dwellings.
